# Future directions: the boundary geometry of the Berggren tree

This is the final version of the research thread's open problems, after three cycles.
Notation follows `Catalog/MachineLearning/Berggren*.lean`: `bil` is the Lorentz form of
signature `(2,1)`, `mA, mB, mC` the Berggren generators, `Gen = A | B | C` the address
alphabet, `dirx, diry` the ideal-point (plot) map, `eu m n = (m²−n², 2mn, m²+n²)` the
Euclid parametrisation, and the *charge* of a triple `v` at a null vector `p` is `−⟨v,p⟩`.

## Status of the previous cycle's five conjectures

Two of them are now theorems, and a third is proved in a corrected form.

| # | Previous conjecture | Outcome |
|---|---------------------|---------|
| 1 | Uniform tangency law `c_v·‖dir v − dir p‖² → 2d/c_p` | **Proved, in exact form**: `chord_times_hyp_eq` shows the product is *constant*, and `contact_order_two_lower` / `contact_order_two_upper` pin the contact order at exactly two. |
| 2 | Spectral rigidity of thin submonoids | Open; see Conjecture A below. |
| 3 | Escape-rate dichotomy for mixed words | Partially proved: `branch_growth_sandwich` gives `5·3^{#B} ≤ c ≤ 5·7^{len}`, so exponential escape is forced by the density of `B`'s. The rationality/irrationality half is open; see Conjecture B. |
| 4 | Star centres are exactly the primitive rational ideal points, with multiplicity | **Multiplicity half now proved.** `star_multiplicity_at_every_primitive_ideal_point` shows the set of spoke charges at every primitive rational ideal point is infinite, and `tree_spoke_charge_spectrum` identifies that set at `(1,0)` *exactly* as `{2n² : n ≥ 1}`. What remains open is only the "at most one curve at a generic irrational point" half; see Conjecture C below. |
| 5 | Charge–depth law: spoke index controls tree depth | **Proved, in corrected form.** The originally conjectured `Θ(log n)` is false as a universal statement (the `mA` branch reaches index `n` only at depth `n−1`). What is true, and now proved, is the universal lower bound `n < 2·3^depth` (`spoke_index_depth_lower_bound`) together with an attaining family: on the hyperbolic branch the index is the Pell number `pell k`, giving `2^k ≤ n < 2·3^k` (`spoke_index_log_sandwich`). |

---

## Conjecture A (Spectral rigidity: `2·□` characterises finite index)

Let `M ⊆ ⟨mA, mB, mC⟩` be a submonoid and let `S(M) ⊆ ℤ_{>0}` be the set of charges
realised at the ideal point `(1,0)` by the orbit `M·root`.  Then `S(M) = {2n² : n ≥ 1}` if
and only if `M` has finite index in the full monoid, and every "thin" submonoid has
`#{d ∈ S(M) : d ≤ X} = o(√X)`.

*The key insight is* that, by `bil_eu_e1`, the charge of a node is `2n²` where `n` is its
smaller Euclid parameter, and by `mA_eu`/`mB_eu`/`mC_eu` the parameter pair evolves by the
ternary tree on coprime pairs; so `S(M)` is the *image of the parameter tree under a
submonoid*, and counting it is an Apollonian-style local–global statistic transplanted to
the Pythagorean setting.

*Why now?* The parameter action is now an explicit, proved intertwining
(`mA_eu`, `mB_eu`, `mC_eu`), so the question is a purely combinatorial one about which
integers appear as second coordinates in a sub-tree of the coprime-pair tree — and it is
computationally testable to `m ≤ 10^6` with the `Gen` alphabet already in the files.

---

## Conjecture B (Arithmetic ⇔ dynamics along an infinite address)

For every infinite address `α : ℕ → Gen` the plotted points of the nodes
`applyGens (take k α) root` converge to a boundary point `ξ(α)`, and

  `ξ(α)` is rational  ⟺  `α` contains only finitely many `B`'s.

Moreover the approach is polynomial (`Θ(k^{-2})`) in the rational case and exponential
in the other.

*The key insight is* that the two parabolic letters conserve a linear functional whose
zero locus is a *rational* null direction, while `B` is hyperbolic with an irrational
axis; so rationality of the limit should be exactly the assertion that the address is
eventually parabolic.

*Why now?* `branch_growth_sandwich` already separates the two growth regimes by the count
of `B`'s, `charge_invariant_under_C` shows the charge is frozen by `C`'s, and
`no_triple_direction_at_pi_div_four` handles the model irrational point.  What remains is
(i) existence of `ξ(α)` — a nested-interval argument for the Stern–Brocot-like ordering of
the coprime-pair tree — and (ii) a Lyapunov estimate for products of the three matrices.

---

## Conjecture C (Multiplicity at an *irrational* boundary point)

The rational half of this conjecture is now a theorem: every primitive rational ideal
point is approached by infinitely many pairwise distinct curves of the plot, one for each
charge `2n²` (`star_multiplicity_at_every_primitive_ideal_point`), and by
`tree_spoke_charge_spectrum` those are the only charges that occur.  What remains is the
contrasting statement:

  every irrational boundary point is approached by **at most one** curve of the plot; more
  precisely, for irrational `ξ` and any `d > 0` there are only finitely many nodes `v` of
  the tree with `c_v·‖dir v − ξ‖² ≤ d`.

*The key insight is* that `chord_times_hyp_eq` turns "lying on a curve into `ξ`" into the
Diophantine condition `|a/c − ξ| ≪ 1/c`, i.e. into an approximation of quality `1/c`
rather than the generic `1/c²`; at a rational point the horocycle supplies infinitely many
such approximations, while at an irrational point their existence would force `ξ` to be
extremely well approximable by the very sparse set of triple directions.

*Why now?* Both inputs exist: `chord_sq_ratio` and `chord_times_hyp_eq` reduce the
multiplicity count to counting integer solutions of `⟨v,p⟩ = −d`, and
`no_triple_direction_at_pi_div_four` shows the technique is already able to certify
irrational boundary points.

---

## Conjecture D (Sharp depth function of a spoke)

Define `D(n)` to be the least depth at which the spoke of index `n` appears, i.e. the least
length of an address `g` with `applyGens g root = eu m n` for some `m`.  Proved here:
`log₃(n/2) < D(n)`, and `D(n) ≤ n − 1` via the `mA` branch.  The conjecture is that the
lower bound is the truth for *every* `n`:

  `D(n) = Θ(log n)`,  i.e.  `D(n) ≤ K · log n` for an absolute constant `K`.

*The key insight is* that the coprime-pair tree of `mA_eu`/`mB_eu`/`mC_eu` is a disguised
Stern–Brocot tree, so the depth of the pair `(m, n)` is a sum of partial quotients of the
continued fraction of `m/n`, and `D(n)` is the minimum of that sum over the admissible
partners `m`.  A uniform `O(log n)` bound is therefore a Zaremba-type statement: it holds
as soon as every `n` admits a partner `m` whose continued fraction has bounded partial
quotients.  Conversely a failure of `D(n) = O(log n)` would produce an explicit family of
integers with no bounded-quotient partner.

*Why now?* The lower bound is proved (`spoke_index_depth_lower_bound`), both extremal
families are proved (`mA_iterate_root_eu` for the slow one, `mB_iterate_root_eu` together
with `pell_ge_two_pow` for the fast one — the Pell branch has all partial quotients equal
to `2`), and the intertwining reduces the general case to a purely continued-fraction
statement about the classical Stern–Brocot tree.  This also turns a question about a
*picture* into a question about Diophantine approximation, which is the kind of bridge the
rest of this development is built on.

---

## Conjecture E (The drawn picture: from the exact relation to the drawn shape)

The exact-relation half is now proved.  With a node of hypotenuse `c` drawn at radius
`r = 1 − 1/c`, `drawn_curve_equation` gives the closed relation
`‖dir v − dir p‖² = 2 d (1 − r)/c_p` between the angular and the radial coordinate along
the spoke of charge `d`, and `draw_tendsto_dir` shows the drawn curve really does run into
the boundary star centre.  The remaining, geometric half is:

  the drawn image of a spoke is, up to a bi-Lipschitz reparametrisation, a genuine
  Euclidean horocycle of the Poincaré disc with curvature a function of `d/c_p` alone, and
  no drawn spoke is an arc of a circle orthogonal to the boundary (no spoke is a geodesic).

*The key insight is* that the proved relation `‖dir v − dir p‖² = 2 d (1 − r)/c_p` is
*exactly* the equation of a Euclidean circle internally tangent to the unit circle at
`dir p`, once the drawn radius `r` is converted to the Poincaré radial coordinate; so the
conjecture is the statement that this coordinate change is bi-Lipschitz on `r ∈ [0,1)`,
which is a one-variable estimate on `1 − 1/c` versus `tanh`.

*Why now?* All the arithmetic input is proved: `drawn_curve_equation` supplies the exact
algebraic relation, `contact_order_two_lower` / `contact_order_two_upper` pin the contact
order at two, which already rules out first-order-contact radii, and `chord_sq_ratio`
separates spokes of different charge quantitatively.

---

## Next-cycle sub-conjectures

Three concrete, falsifiable statements to attack immediately, in increasing difficulty.

**C1 (finiteness at a quadratic irrational).**  For the hyperbolic ideal point
`ξ = √2/2` and every `d > 0` the set of Pythagorean triples with
`c·‖dir v − (ξ, ξ)‖² ≤ d` is finite.  This is the smallest interesting instance of
Conjecture C, and `mB_ray_bound` already gives the matching exponential upper estimate on
the one branch that does approach `ξ`, so the content is a lower bound of the same shape
for every other branch.

**E1 (no spoke is a geodesic).**  For every `d > 0` and every star centre `p`, the drawn
spoke of charge `d` is not contained in any circle orthogonal to the unit circle.  By
`drawn_curve_equation` this reduces to showing that a three-point condition on the exact
relation is inconsistent, i.e. to a polynomial identity in `d`, `c_p` and two hypotenuses.

**A1 (spoke charges of the `mC`-free submonoid).**  The submonoid generated by `mA` and
`mB` alone realises exactly the charges `2n²` with `n` a numerator of a continued fraction
with all partial quotients equal to `1` or `2` — i.e. the Stern–Brocot subtree cut out by
the two letters — and therefore `#{d ≤ X in that spectrum} = X^{θ+o(1)}` with `θ < 1/2`.
This is the first testable case of Conjecture A, and `mA_eu` / `mB_eu` already exhibit the
submonoid action on Euclid pairs as the required continued-fraction dynamics.

# Future Directions — EML exp–log duality

Derived from the analysis and adversarial review of the results now proved in
`Catalog/Probability/EMLExpLogDuality.lean` and
`Catalog/Probability/EMLScalingGroupDuality.lean`.

## What survived, what did not

* **Survived (0 sorries).** The scaling group acts simply transitively on
  ordered pairs of distinct points of `(0, ∞)`, so the EML state space is a
  torsor over it (`ScalingMap.existsUnique_of_pair`). The EML generator space carries a Lie algebra
  structure isomorphic (explicitly, `emlMatrixEquiv`) to `𝔞𝔣𝔣(1)` in its faithful
  `2 × 2` representation; it is solvable of derived length two and *not*
  nilpotent; the exp–log change of variables intertwines the affine and EML
  vector-field commutators; the flow of every EML field is a scaling
  transformation `y ↦ c y^k`; the exponential map is surjective exactly onto
  the identity component; globally `AffMap ≃* ScalingMap`; and the catalog
  operation `eml x y = exp x - log y` intertwines the scaling action on states
  with an affine action on EML values.
* **Needed a different definition.** The naive statement "`g ↦ affField g` is a
  Lie algebra isomorphism onto affine vector fields" is *false* with the
  standard commutator convention `⁅f∂, h∂⁆ = (f h' - h f')∂`: it is an
  anti-isomorphism (`affField_vfBracket`).  The correct statement uses the flip
  `(a, b) ↦ (-a, b)`, an isomorphism onto the opposite algebra
  (`affField_flip_vfBracket`).  This sign is intrinsic (left versus right
  actions), not a bookkeeping accident.
* **False as first conjectured.** "The scaling group is torsion free / the
  exponential map is surjective."  Both fail: `y ↦ c/y` is an involution
  (`ScalingMap.sq_eq_one_iff`) and lies outside the image of `emlExpMap`
  (`emlExpMap_not_surjective`).  The group has two components and only the
  identity component is exponential.

## Conjecture 1 (rigidity of the EML realization) — *core step closed in cycle 2*

Every two-dimensional real Lie algebra of real-analytic vector fields on
`(0, ∞)` that contains the Euler field `y ∂_y` and acts locally transitively is
carried onto `{ y (a log y + b) ∂_y }` by a real-analytic diffeomorphism of
`(0, ∞)`; in particular the `log` in `emlField` is *forced*, not chosen.

*The key insight is* that in the eigenbasis of `ad` of the Euler field the
second generator must satisfy the linear ODE `y f' - f = f`, whose only
solutions are `y(a log y + b)` — so the logarithm is the unique solution of a
first-order rigidity equation rather than a modelling convention.

*Why now?* The formalization already contains the two ingredients needed for a
Lean proof: `emlField_hasDerivAt` (the derivative of the candidate generator)
and `emlField_vfBracket` (the closure relation).  What is missing is only a
uniqueness argument for the ODE, for which Mathlib's `ODE_solution_unique` is
available.

## Conjecture 2 (log-normal orbit theorem and its curvature)

The scaling group acts simply transitively on the family of log-normal laws with
positive scale parameter, and under this identification the Fisher–Rao metric of
the log-normal family is a left-invariant metric on `Aff⁺(ℝ)` of constant
negative curvature.  Falsifiable form: the Fisher information matrix of
`LogNormal(μ, σ)` is `diag(σ^{-2}, 2σ^{-2})`, whose associated metric has
Gaussian curvature `-1/2`.

*The key insight is* that `eml_scaling_affine` already exhibits the scaling group
acting affinely on log-scale statistics, so the log-normal family is a *torsor*
over the group; the Fisher metric, being invariant, is then determined by a
single number at the identity.

*Why now?* `EMLInformationGeometry.lean` in this catalog shows that the naive
one-neuron exp-log family has a *singular* Fisher matrix because the
exponential scale cancels under normalization.  The present duality explains
why: that model quotients by the very translation subgroup whose orbit direction
the metric would have measured.  The conjecture predicts that restoring the
missing direction (the power parameter `k`) makes the metric nondegenerate.

## Conjecture 3 (equivariance of large deviations)

For i.i.d. positive random variables, the Gärtner–Ellis rate function transforms
under the scaling action `Y ↦ c Y^k` by
`I ↦ (x ↦ I((x - log c)/k))` in log coordinates, i.e. the Legendre transform
conjugates `cgfAction` to the *inverse* affine substitution.  Falsifiable: the
identity must hold for every finitely supported law, including `k < 0`, where
the Legendre transform is taken over the reflected domain.

*The key insight is* that `cgfAction` is an affine action with a cocycle term
`s log c`, and Legendre duality turns a cocycle in the argument into a
translation in the value — so the entire large-deviation machinery is
equivariant for a *non-abelian* group, not just for the translations usually
considered.

*Why now?* `discreteCGF_scaling` and `cgfAction_mul` are proved here for finite
state spaces, which is exactly the setting in which Cramér's theorem is already
formalizable; the remaining step is a Legendre-transform lemma.

## Conjecture 4 (no finite-dimensional faithful unitary representation) — *closed in cycle 2 for the skew-symmetric (compact) case*

The EML algebra admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation by
skew-adjoint operators; equivalently, every finite-dimensional complex
representation has `T` acting nilpotently, so the pure-scaling generator is
never diagonalizable in a faithful unitary model.

*The key insight is* that `⁅D, T⁆ = T` forces `T` to be an eigenvector of
`ad D` with nonzero eigenvalue, and `not_isNilpotent` together with Lie's
theorem then pins every irreducible finite-dimensional representation to be a
character killing `T`.

*Why now?* Both hypotheses are now formal: `lie_D_T` and
`derivedSeries_two_eq_bot` give solvability, so Mathlib's Lie-theoretic
machinery (`LieAlgebra.IsSolvable`, weight theory) can be applied directly to
`EMLGen` rather than to an abstract two-dimensional algebra.

## Conjecture 5 (cohomological obstruction to a canonical EML normalization)

The map `d ↦ (s ↦ s log d.coeff)` is a nontrivial one-cocycle for the scaling
group acting on functions `ℝ → ℝ`; consequently there is no
scaling-equivariant normalization of cumulant generating functions, and no
canonical choice of "unit of scale" for EML states.

*The key insight is* that the cocycle is a coboundary if and only if the
character `d ↦ log d.coeff` extends to a group homomorphism invariant under the
power action, which fails precisely because `⁅D, T⁆ = T`.

*Why now?* `cgfAction_mul` is the cocycle identity in formal form; deciding
triviality only requires exhibiting or excluding a fixed function, a statement
of first-order arithmetic over the reals.

## Three concrete next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. **(SC1 — closed during this cycle)** `derivedSeries ℝ EMLGen 1 = shiftIdeal`:
   the derived algebra is *exactly* the pure-scaling line
   (`derivedSeries_one_eq_shiftIdeal`).  Its replacement:
   **(SC1′)** the quotient `EMLGen ⧸ shiftIdeal` is the one-dimensional abelian
   algebra, and the resulting short exact sequence of Lie algebras is
   non-split *as a sequence of groups after exponentiation* precisely on the
   component `k < 0`.
2. **(SC2)** The centralizer of `emlField g` in the space of `C¹` vector fields
   on `(0, ∞)` is one-dimensional for `g.scale ≠ 0` and infinite-dimensional for
   `g.scale = 0` — a sharp dichotomy detecting the dilation part.
3. **(SC3)** `ScalingMap ≃* AffMap` is the *unique* topological group
   isomorphism between the two groups up to inner automorphisms and the
   reflection `k ↦ k`, `c ↦ c⁻¹`; i.e. `Out(Aff⁺(ℝ))` is trivial while
   `Out(Aff(ℝ))` has order two.


---

# Cycle 2 update (file `Catalog/Probability/EMLLieRigidity.lean`)

The second pass through the loop closed, with complete Lean proofs and no
`sorry`, the following items from the list above.

* **Conjecture 4, skew-symmetric case — proved.**
  `EMLLieRigidity.no_faithful_skew_representation`: no representation of the EML
  generator algebra by skew-symmetric real matrices is faithful; the
  pure-scaling generator always acts by zero.  The mechanism turned out to be
  much more elementary than the weight-theoretic argument anticipated above: the
  identity `tr(⁅A,B⁆ · B) = 0` (`trace_lie_mul_self`, true for *all* square
  matrices) turns the relation `⁅A,B⁆ = B` into `tr(B²) = 0`, and the trace form
  is negative definite on skew-symmetric matrices.  So the obstruction is a
  *quadratic form* obstruction, not a representation-theoretic one — a strictly
  stronger and more portable statement than the one conjectured.
* **Two by-products, also proved.**  In *every* finite-dimensional
  representation the pure-scaling generator is trace-nilpotent
  (`rep_shift_trace_pow_eq_zero`: `tr((ρT)^k) = 0` for all `k ≥ 1`, via
  `⁅A, Bᵏ⁆ = k·Bᵏ`) and singular (`rep_shift_det_not_isUnit`; invertibility
  would give `A - B A B⁻¹ = 1`, whose trace reads `0 = n`).
* **Conjecture 1, core ODE step — proved.**  `EMLLieRigidity.emlField_rigidity`:
  a differentiable field `F ∂` on `(0, ∞)` with
  `⁅(y log y) ∂, F ∂⁆ = -F ∂` satisfies `F y = F 1 · y`, i.e. it is exactly
  `emlField (0, F 1)`; `affField_rigidity` is the affine counterpart on `ℝ`.
  The `log` in `emlField` is therefore *forced*.  The subtlety that had to be
  handled is that the ODE degenerates at the fixed point of the dilation
  (`x = 0`, resp. `y = 1`): the derivative condition only holds off that point
  and the two components must be glued by continuity
  (`const_of_mul_deriv_eq_zero`, `const_of_deriv_eq_zero_punctured`).
* **SC1′, first half — proved.**  `quotient_isLieAbelian` and
  `quotient_mk_D_ne_zero`: the quotient `EMLGen ⧸ shiftIdeal` is a nonzero
  abelian Lie algebra, and `lieHom_abelian_factors` shows the scale character
  `scaleChar : EMLGen →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ ℝ` is *universal* among maps to abelian algebras.

## Three next-cycle sub-conjectures  *(NC1 closed in cycle 3; NC3 refuted in cycle 3)*

1. **(NC1 — from trace to nilpotency; dimension two already proved.)**  In every
   finite-dimensional real representation `ρ` of `EMLGen` of dimension `n`,
   `(ρ T)^n = 0` — established here for `n = 2`
   (`rep_dim_two_shift_isNilpotent`, via Cayley–Hamilton) and conjectured in
   general; the shift
   ideal acts by nilpotent operators, so the only irreducible finite-dimensional
   representations are the one-dimensional characters `g ↦ c · g.scale`.
   *The key insight is* that `rep_shift_trace_pow_eq_zero` already gives every
   power sum `p_k = tr(B^k) = 0`, and in characteristic zero Newton's identities
   convert vanishing power sums into `charpoly B = X^n`, which is nilpotency.
   *Why now?*  The power sums are formal; the missing ingredient is the Newton
   identity bridge between `Matrix.trace (B ^ k)` and
   `Matrix.charpoly`, for which Mathlib has both the symmetric-function API and
   `LinearMap.isNilpotent_iff_charpoly`.
2. **(NC2 — global rigidity.)**  Every two-dimensional real Lie algebra of `C¹`
   vector fields on `(0, ∞)` containing the EML dilation field `y log y ∂` and
   acting locally transitively is carried onto `{ y (a log y + b) ∂ }` by a
   diffeomorphism of `(0, ∞)`.  *The key insight is* that `emlField_rigidity`
   pins the eigenvalue `-1` eigenspace of `ad` to be exactly the line
   `ℝ · (y ∂)`; a `C¹` conjugation argument then transports an arbitrary such
   algebra onto the standard one.  *Why now?*  The eigenspace computation — the
   hard analytic step — is now a theorem rather than a hope; the remainder is
   the flow-box theorem for a nonvanishing `C¹` field.
3. **(NC3 — centralizer dichotomy, restated from SC2.)**  The centralizer of
   `emlField g` inside the `C¹` vector fields on `(0, ∞)` is one-dimensional
   when `g.scale ≠ 0` and infinite-dimensional when `g.scale = 0`.
   *The key insight is* that the centralizer equation is the same singular first
   order ODE treated in cycle 2, but with eigenvalue `0` instead of `-1`, so the
   glueing lemma `const_of_deriv_eq_zero_punctured` applies verbatim and the
   dichotomy is exactly the presence or absence of the singular point.
   *Why now?*  Both halves reduce to lemmas already proved here; only the
   dimension count of the solution space remains.

# Cycle 3 update (file `Catalog/Probability/EMLNilpotentCentralizer.lean`)

Cycle 3 attacked the two open sub-conjectures NC1 and NC3 of cycle 2.  One was
proved in a stronger form than conjectured; the other turned out to be *false*
in exactly one half, and has been replaced by the correct theorem.

* **NC1 — proved, in full and by a different mechanism.**
  `EMLNilpotentCentralizer.rep_shift_isNilpotent` and
  `rep_shift_pow_card_eq_zero`: in *every* finite-dimensional real
  representation `ρ` of dimension `n`, `ρ T` is nilpotent and `(ρ T) ^ n = 0`.
  Cycle 2 had only the case `n = 2` and proposed to go through Newton's
  identities applied to the vanishing power traces.  That route is unnecessary.
  The relation `⁅A, B⁆ = B` makes every nonzero power `B ^ (k+1)` an eigenvector
  of the *single* linear operator `ad A` on the finite-dimensional space of
  matrices, with eigenvalue `k + 1` (`EMLLieRigidity.lie_pow_eq_nsmul`).  Since
  an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space has only finitely many
  eigenvalues (`Module.End.finite_hasEigenvalue`), almost all of these powers
  vanish, i.e. `isNilpotent_of_lie_eq_self`.  The sharp exponent then comes from
  `charpoly B = X ^ n` (`Matrix.isNilpotent_charpoly_sub_pow_of_isNilpotent`
  plus the fact that `ℝ[X]` is reduced) and Cayley–Hamilton.  The argument is
  *purely spectral* and uses no property of `ℝ` beyond characteristic zero.
* **By-product.**  `rep_dim_one_eq_scaleChar_smul`: every one-dimensional
  representation is `g ↦ g.scale • ρ D`, i.e. a multiple of the scale character
  — the representation-theoretic shadow of the abelian quotient
  `EMLGen ⧸ shiftIdeal ≅ ℝ` established in cycle 2.
* **NC3 — first half proved, second half refuted.**
  `emlField_centralizer`: for *every* `g ≠ 0` the centralizer of `emlField g`
  inside the differentiable vector fields on `(0, ∞)` is exactly the line
  `ℝ · emlField g`; `centralizer_pairwise_dependent` states the resulting
  one-dimensionality in elementary terms, and `emlField_ne_zero_on_Ioi` shows
  the line is nonzero.  So the conjectured *dichotomy* does not exist.  What
  went wrong in the guess: for `g.scale = 0` the centralizer equation is
  `b (y F' - F) = 0`, the Euler equation, whose differentiable solutions on the
  connected half line `(0, ∞)` are only the scaling fields `F y = c y`
  (`emlField_centralizer_of_scale_eq_zero`).  The intuition that a vanishing
  eigenvalue creates a large solution space is wrong here because the field
  `b y ∂` has *no* singular point on `(0, ∞)` — the extra freedom one expects
  would live at a zero of the field, and there is none.
* **The singular case is the hard one.**  For `g.scale ≠ 0` the field vanishes
  at `p = exp(-g.shift / g.scale)`, the fixed point of its flow.  The quotient
  `F / emlField g` is locally constant on `(0, p)` and on `(p, ∞)` but is *not*
  continuous at `p`, so the glueing lemma of cycle 2
  (`const_of_deriv_eq_zero_punctured`, which needed continuity) does not apply.
  The new lemma `const_glue_of_differentiableAt` glues by comparing the one-sided
  limits of the *difference quotient* of `F` at `p`: both equal `deriv F p`, and
  they compute `c₁ · (emlField g)' p` and `c₂ · (emlField g)' p` with
  `(emlField g)' p = g.scale ≠ 0`.  This is a reusable "removable singularity of
  an eigenvector equation" lemma.

## Three next-cycle sub-conjectures

1. **(NC4 — the whole representation is nilpotent-by-abelian, quantitatively.)**
   In every finite-dimensional real representation `ρ` of `EMLGen` of dimension
   `n`, the image `ρ (shiftIdeal)` is simultaneously strictly triangularizable,
   and `ρ D` is conjugate to a matrix whose diagonal blocks are those of a
   semisimple operator with integer eigenvalue *differences*; equivalently
   `V = ⨁_{j} V_j` with `ρ T : V_j → V_{j+1}`.
   *The key insight is* that cycle 3 gives nilpotency of `ρ T` for free, and
   nilpotency plus the eigenvector relation `⁅ρ D, ρ T⁆ = ρ T` is exactly the
   hypothesis of the weight decomposition for the generalized eigenspaces of
   `ad (ρ D)`.  *Why now?*  The missing analytic input (nilpotency) is a
   theorem, and Mathlib has generalized eigenspace decompositions for
   endomorphisms of finite-dimensional spaces.
2. **(NC5 — global centralizer in the group picture.)**  *[settled in cycle 4: the abelian half is proved, the identification with the one-parameter subgroup is false — see below]*  The centralizer of a
   non-identity element of `ScalingMap` is abelian, and equals the image of the
   one-parameter subgroup through it precisely when its exponent is not `1`;
   for exponent `1` (pure dilations `y ↦ c y`) it is the full dilation
   subgroup.  *The key insight is* that the infinitesimal statement proved in
   cycle 3 (centralizer of a field is the line it spans) should integrate to the
   group level, the exceptional case being the one where the flow has no fixed
   point in `(0, ∞)`.  *Why now?*  `EMLScalingGroupDuality` already has the
   group law, the trivial-centre theorem and the classification of involutions,
   so the computation is a finite case analysis on `(coeff, expo)`.
3. **(NC6 — the trace obstruction is the only obstruction.)**  A finite
   -dimensional real Lie algebra `L` admits a surjection onto `EMLGen` if and
   only if `L` is not perfect and its derived algebra contains an
   `ad`-eigenvector of nonzero eigenvalue.  *The key insight is* that
   `scaleChar` is the universal map to an abelian algebra (cycle 2) and
   `isNilpotent_of_lie_eq_self` (cycle 3) says the eigenvector is nilpotent in
   every representation, so the obstruction is intrinsic and not
   representation-dependent.  *Why now?*  Both halves are already formalized as
   standalone theorems; only the assembly into an iff remains.

# Cycle 4 update (file `Catalog/Probability/EMLGroupCentralizer.lean`)

Cycle 4 integrates the infinitesimal centralizer theorem of cycle 3 to the group
level and settles NC5 — half of it as conjectured, half of it not.

* **One identity governs everything.**  `AffMap.commute_iff`: two affine maps
  commute iff `g.trans (f.lin − 1) = f.trans (g.lin − 1)`.  The linear parts
  commute automatically, so the entire commutation problem in a nonabelian
  two-dimensional group collapses to one bilinear equation.
* **NC5, the abelian half — proved.**  `AffMap.centralizer_commutative` and its
  transport `ScalingMap.centralizer_commutative`: the centralizer of any
  non-identity element is abelian.  This is the group shadow of cycle 3's
  one-dimensionality of the infinitesimal centralizer.
* **NC5, the identification with a one-parameter subgroup — false.**  For
  `f.lin ≠ 1` the centralizer is the *stabilizer of the fixed point*
  `x* = f.trans / (1 − f.lin)` (`AffMap.commute_iff_fixes_fixedPoint`,
  `ScalingMap.commute_iff_fixes_fixedPoint`), a group with two connected
  components.  `ScalingMap.centralizer_has_negative_expo_element` exhibits the
  inversion `y ↦ 1/y` inside the centralizer of `y ↦ y²`; since every element in
  the image of the exponential map has positive exponent
  (`EMLExpLogDuality.emlExpMap_expo_pos`), the centralizer is strictly larger
  than the flow through the element.  The guess failed for a *topological*
  reason, not an algebraic one: passing from the Lie algebra to the group can
  only recover the identity component.
* **The exceptional case behaves as predicted.**  For a nontrivial translation
  (`f.lin = 1`, `f.trans ≠ 0`, i.e. a pure dilation `y ↦ c y` on the scaling
  side) the centralizer is exactly the translation subgroup
  (`AffMap.commute_iff_of_lin_eq_one`) — connected, and equal to the
  one-parameter subgroup.  So the dichotomy in the *global* picture is between
  "has a fixed point in `(0, ∞)`" and "has none", which is precisely the
  distinction that cycle 3 showed is invisible infinitesimally.

## Open conjectures after cycle 4

NC4 and NC6 above remain open, and cycle 4 suggests one more:

**(NC7 — component count is the only global invariant.)**  For every
`d : ScalingMap` with `d ≠ 1`, the centralizer of `d` has exactly two connected
components when `d.expo ≠ 1` and one when `d.expo = 1`; equivalently, the map
`e ↦ sign e.expo` is a surjection from the centralizer onto `{±1}` in the first
case and constant in the second.  *The key insight is* that cycle 4 identifies
the centralizer with a point stabilizer `≅ ℝˣ` respectively with the translation
group `≅ ℝ`, and `ℝˣ` has two components while `ℝ` has one; the whole statement
therefore reduces to the classification already proved, plus a connectedness
computation.  *Why now?*  Both centralizers are now described by explicit
equations in `(coeff, expo)`, so the topology can be read off a homeomorphism
with `ℝˣ` or `ℝ` rather than from an abstract Lie-group argument.

# Future directions — snakes and coils in the hypercube (cycle 4)

All Lean files of this thread live in `Catalog/Novelty/` (plus the base chain in
`Catalog/Computation/SnakeInTheBox.lean` and `Catalog/Computation/SnakeMax.lean`),
compile end-to-end, and contain no `sorry`, no `native_decide` and no extra
axioms: every headline theorem depends only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`,
`Quot.sound`.

## What earlier cycles established

| file | content |
|------|---------|
| `Catalog/Novelty/HypercubeInducedDegree.lean` | The counting chain generalised away from snakes: **any** `S ⊆ Q n` with maximum induced degree `d` obeys `(2n - d)\|S\| ≤ n 2ⁿ`; for `d = 2`, `\|S\| ≤ 3·2^(n-2)`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/HypercubeCoil.lean` | **Coils** (induced cycles): evenness, exact classification in dimensions two and three, the lift `Coil n L → Coil (n+1) (L+2)`, `maxCoil` with `2n ≤ maxCoil n ≤ 3·2^(n-2)`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeConcat.lean` | **Concatenation**: `maxLen m + maxLen n ≤ maxLen (m+n)`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeSeed.lean`, `SnakeSeedSeven.lean` | Kernel-verified snakes of lengths `26` in `Q 6` and `47` in `Q 7`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/CoilRectangle.lean` | **Rectangle**: `Snake m L → Snake n M → Coil (m+n) (2L+2M)`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeOutsideStructure.lean` | Parity and companion structure of the outer boundary of a snake. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeSymmetry.lean` | The hyperoctahedral action, path reversal, and the **support theorem** `L ≤ maxLen #dirs`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeQuadratic.lean` | Doubling recursion and the quadratic bound `n² ≤ 5·maxLen n`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeGridComb.lean` | **Product theorem** `maxLen m · maxLen n ≤ 2·maxLen (m+n)` and `23^⌊n/7⌋ ≤ maxLen n`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeSupport.lean` | `maxLen 0 = 0`, `maxLen 1 = 1`, **strict monotonicity** of `maxLen`, and the **full-support theorem**. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeGrowthConstant.lean` | **The snake constant exists**: `(maxLen n)^(1/n) → snakeGrowth`, with `23^(1/7) ≤ snakeGrowth ≤ 2`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/CoilGrowth.lean` | **Coils grow at exactly the snake rate**: `(maxCoil n)^(1/n) → snakeGrowth`. |

## What this cycle added

| file | content |
|------|---------|
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeCombSharp.lean` | **The comb bound without rounding.** `maxLen_comb_sharp` keeps the full output `⌊maxLen m/2⌋·(maxLen n + 2) + maxLen n` of the comb, giving `maxLen_mul_le_sharp : maxLen m · maxLen n + 2·maxLen m + maxLen n ≤ 2·maxLen (m+n) + 2`, strictly stronger than the previous cycle's product theorem (this closes sub-conjecture 3 of cycle 3). Two general consequences are isolated: `maxLen_step_of_seed` (one snake of `Q k` with `N` even edges multiplies the maximal length by `N/2 + 1` every `k` dimensions — compare `Snake.lift2`, which only *adds* two) and `maxLen_exp_of_seed` (hence `maxLen n ≥ (N/2+1)^⌊n/k⌋`), together with the analytic counterpart `snakeGrowth_ge_of_maxLen`: *any* verified snake bounds the growth constant from below by `(N/2)^(1/k)`. |
| `Catalog/Novelty/SnakeSeedEight.lean` | **An explicit snake of length 86 in `Q 8`**, found by depth-first search with restarts and verified by kernel computation (`decide`, no `native_decide`) — the first eight-dimensional seed of the thread, and even, so the sharp comb applies to it with no loss. Instantiating the two general lemmas: `maxLen_exponential_eight : 8 ≤ n → 44^⌊n/8⌋ ≤ maxLen n`, `snakeGrowth_ge_eight : 43^(1/8) ≤ snakeGrowth` and `one_point_six_lt_snakeGrowth : 1.6 < snakeGrowth`, packaged with the counting ceiling in `maxLen_picture_eight` and `snakeGrowth_bracket_sharp`. |

Numerically the bracket for the growth constant moved from
`[1.5637…, 2]` to `[1.6003…, 2]`, and the exponential lower bound from
`23^⌊n/7⌋` to `44^⌊n/8⌋`; sub-conjecture 2 of the previous cycle (a better
base from a better seed) is therefore realised, in the weaker form `86` rather
than the optimum `98`.

## Conjecture 1 (the weighted boundary count beats density 1/2)

> There is an absolute `c > 0` such that every snake `S` of `Q n` satisfies
> `|S| ≤ (1/2 - c)·2ⁿ`; equivalently `snakeGrowth ≤ 2 - c'` for some `c' > 0`.

**The key insight is** that the boundary is not spread evenly: by
`Snake.exists_companion` every corner of a snake produces an outside vertex of
induced degree at least two, and by `Snake.outside_nbr_structure` the snake
neighbours of an outside vertex have indices of one parity, pairwise at least
two apart and pairwise at Hamming distance exactly two — so a high-degree
outside vertex forces a packing of distance-two pairs inside one parity class,
which the unweighted count in `Snake.boundary_upper` throws away.

**Why now?** `snakeGrowth` is a definable real number with a *two-sided*
numerical bracket `[1.6003…, 2]`, so "beating density 1/2" is a single clean
inequality about one constant; and `snakeGrowth_ge_of_maxLen` shows the lower
half of the bracket will keep rising with every new seed, which makes the
question of whether the *upper* half can be lowered the only remaining
qualitative unknown.

## Conjecture 2 (the sharp comb is still not sharp: the additive defect grows)

> `2·maxLen (m+n) - maxLen m · maxLen n - 2·maxLen m - maxLen n → ∞` as
> `m, n → ∞`; equivalently the sequence `(maxLen k / 2)^{1/k}` is *strictly*
> increasing, and `snakeGrowth > ((maxLen k)/2)^{1/k}` for every `k`.

**The key insight is** that the comb never leaves the grid spanned by the two
factor snakes, and the longest induced path of an `a × b` grid has about `ab/2`
vertices; every genuine improvement must use vertices `(x, y)` whose first block
`x` is off the first snake, and those exist in abundance because a snake omits
more than `2^(n-2)` vertices (`Snake.omits_lt`).

**Why now?** Fekete's lemma identifies `snakeGrowth` with the *supremum* of
`(maxLen k / 2)^{1/k}`, and `maxLen_mul_le_sharp` now quantifies the defect of
the comb exactly (the two linear terms), so the conjecture is a statement about
a concrete, formally defined quantity rather than about "a construction".

## Conjecture 3 (coils cost at most four edges, exactly)

> `maxLen n - 2 ≤ maxCoil n ≤ maxLen n + 2` for all `n ≥ 3`.

The upper half is proved (`maxCoil_le_maxLen_add_two`) and the asymptotic form
of the lower half is a theorem (`maxCoil_rpow_tendsto`: both sides have growth
constant `snakeGrowth`). What remains is the exact, non-asymptotic statement.

**The key insight is** that the rectangle construction closes *two* snakes into
a cycle at no cost, so the obstruction to closing a *single* snake is purely
local at its endpoints: the two ends of a maximal snake are at Hamming distance
at least two and must be joined by a short path avoiding the snake's
neighbourhood.

**Why now?** The sandwich `maxLen (n-3) ≤ maxCoil n ≤ 3·maxLen n` shows nothing
exponential is lost, so the remaining gap is a bounded additive constant —
exactly the regime where the explicit small-dimension data (`maxCoil 2 = 4`,
`maxCoil 3 = 6`, `maxLen 2 = 2`, `maxLen 3 = 4`) can be combined with a local
endpoint-closing lemma.

## Conjecture 4 (a per-dimension doubling, not a per-block one)

> `maxLen (n+1) ≥ (3/2)·maxLen n` for all sufficiently large `n`; in particular
> the increment `maxLen (n+1) - maxLen n` tends to infinity.

**The key insight is** that all the exponential growth proved so far is
*block-averaged*: `maxLen_step_of_seed` multiplies by `N/2 + 1` only every `k`
dimensions, and between two multiples of `k` the development still falls back on
`Snake.lift2`, which adds two edges. A reflected-Gray-code-style construction
`s(n+1) ≥ 2 s(n) - c` would interpolate, and the chord condition it must
maintain is exactly the parity-separated distance condition
`Snake.three_le_hammingDist`.

**Why now?** Strict monotonicity of `maxLen` (cycle 3) rules out plateaus, the
full-support theorem says a maximal snake really does use each new coordinate,
and `maxLen_step_of_seed` isolates in one line where the factor is bought — so
the missing statement is precisely a one-dimension version of a lemma that is
already in the file, with the same shape.

## Conjecture 5 (exact values in dimensions four and eight)

> `Nonempty (Snake 4 L) ↔ L ≤ 7`, i.e. `maxLen 4 = 7`; and `maxLen 8 = 98`.

The counting bound gives only `L ≤ 9` in dimension four, and the seed of this
cycle gives `86 ≤ maxLen 8 ≤ 190`.

**The key insight is** that the symmetry reduction makes the four-dimensional
search finite and small: by `Snake.translate` one may assume `v 0 = 0`, by
`Snake.permute` that the first step flips coordinate `0`, and consecutive steps
flip different coordinates, so a snake of length `8` in `Q 4` is one of at most
`4·3⁶ = 2916` direction sequences up to symmetry — a single decidable statement.

**Why now?** Both normalisations are theorems (`exists_snake_base_zero`,
`Snake.permute`), the kernel has just been shown to verify an `87`-vertex
eight-dimensional snake by `decide` in about a minute, and `maxLen_injective`
means each new exact value pins down a distinct dimension.

## Three concrete sub-conjectures for the next cycle

1. **A strictly better ceiling.** `snakeGrowth ≤ 2 - 10^{-3}`: formalise a
   weighted `boundary_upper` in which every outside vertex of induced degree
   `d ≥ 2` is charged `n - (d - 1)` instead of `n`, and combine it with a count
   of the corners of a snake (each corner yields a companion of degree `≥ 2`).
2. **Close the seed gap.** A kernel-verified snake of length `98` in `Q 8`, or of
   length `50` in `Q 7`, raises the proved bracket to `snakeGrowth ≥ 49^{1/8} =
   1.6266…` with no change to any proof: `maxLen_exp_of_seed` and
   `snakeGrowth_ge_of_maxLen` take the seed as a parameter. The obstruction is
   purely the search; the plateau at `86` reported in `ComputationalEvidence.md`
   suggests a symmetry-guided or SAT-based search instead of restart DFS.
3. **A three-factor comb.** Iterate the sharp comb over three blocks at once and
   compare with the two-block iteration: the conjecture is that the three-block
   version loses only one additive constant rather than two, giving
   `maxLen (k+l+m) ≥ maxLen k · maxLen l · maxLen m / 4 + …` and hence a bracket
   improvement that does not need a new seed.

# Future directions

The formalization in `Catalog/Shared/SolomonZeta/` (mirrored in the buildable library
`Shared/SolomonZeta/`) now contains, all machine-checked and free of `sorry`:

* the effective coefficient formula
  `#Aut(X) · #{N ≤ M : M/N ≅ X} = Σ_{Y ≤ X} μ(Y, X) · #Hom(M, Y)`
  (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_eq_mobiusWeight`), with Möbius invariance under order isomorphisms
  (`mu_orderIso`) and the coprime Euler factorization (`mobiusWeight_prod_of_coprime`);
* **[settled this cycle, was C1/C3]** the Gaussian-binomial evaluation for elementary abelian
  quotient types: `#GL_d(𝔽_p) · #{N ≤ ℤⁿ : ℤⁿ/N ≅ (ℤ/p)^d} = ∏_{i<d}(pⁿ - p^i)`
  (`card_GL_mul_quotIsoCount_elementaryAbelian`, `mobiusWeight_elementaryAbelian`), proved from a
  rank duality between spanning columns and independent rows
  (`span_cols_eq_top_iff_linearIndependent_rows`);
* **[settled this cycle, was C2]** the full cyclic formula
  `φ(m) · #{N ≤ ℤⁿ : ℤⁿ/N ≅ ℤ/m} = Σ_{d ∣ m} μ(d)·(m/d)ⁿ = J_n(m)`
  (`totient_mul_quotIsoCount_zmod_eq_jordan`), i.e. the incidence-algebra Möbius function of the
  submodule poset is carried onto the arithmetic Möbius function
  (`solomonCyclicCoeff_eq_moebius_mul_pow`);
* **[new]** the local (Nakayama) collapse over a commutative local order with finite residue
  field `k`, `q = #k`: for every finite `R`-module `X`,
  `Σ_{Y ≤ X} μ(Y, X)·#Hom(Rⁿ, Y) = (∏_{i<d}(qⁿ - q^i)) · #(𝔪X)ⁿ`, `d = dim_k X/𝔪X`
  (`mobiusWeight_free_local`), hence the coefficient of a free lattice depends on the quotient
  type only through `(#𝔪X, dim_k X/𝔪X)` (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_free_local_congr`);
* **[new]** its specialisation to the maximal order `ℤ_p` of `ℚ_p`
  (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_padic_free`);
* **[new]** Hall's formula over `ℤ`: for an arbitrary finite abelian `p`-group `X` of exponent
  dividing `pᵉ`, `#Aut(X)·#{N ≤ ℤⁿ : ℤⁿ/N ≅ X} = (∏_{i<d}(pⁿ - p^i))·#(pX)ⁿ`
  (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_pGroup`), via a nilpotent-ideal Nakayama lemma
  (`eq_top_of_sup_smul_eq_top`) that dispenses with the local hypothesis.

The record below states what was closed this cycle (D1) and the four conjectures that remain
open; each is phrased so that a formal proof (or a counterexample) is a well-defined Lean goal
on top of the verified machinery above.

---

## D1 (settled). Hall's formula for arbitrary finite abelian `p`-groups

**Theorem** (`autCard_mul_quotIsoCount_pGroup`, `Catalog/Shared/SolomonZeta/AbelianPGroup.lean`).
For a finite abelian `p`-group `X` of exponent dividing `pᵉ` and every `n`,
`#Aut(X) · #{N ≤ ℤⁿ : ℤⁿ/N ≅ X} = (∏_{i<d}(pⁿ - p^i)) · #(pX)ⁿ`, `d = dim_{𝔽_p} X/pX`.
So the weighted coefficient depends on the isomorphism type of `X` only through the pair
`(#pX, dim_{𝔽_p} X/pX)`; for `X` of type `λ` this is `p^{n(|λ|-d)}·∏_{i<d}(pⁿ - p^i)`.

*The key insight was* that the Nakayama step needs no local ring: if an ideal `I` satisfies
`Iᵉ·X = 0` and `Y + I·X = X`, then `Y = X` (`eq_top_of_sup_smul_eq_top`), so the Möbius sum over
the submodule poset of `X` collapses to the Frattini quotient `X/pX` rescaled by `#(pX)ⁿ`.

*Remaining sub-conjecture.* Identify `#pX = p^{|λ|-d}` and `d = #parts(λ)` for `X` presented as
`∏ ℤ/p^{λᵢ}`, turning the theorem into the classical statement in terms of partitions, and
deduce the global (all primes at once) formula by the verified Euler factorization.

## D2. Group rings over `ℤ_p` are local for `p`-groups

**Conjecture.** For a finite `p`-group `G` the group ring `Λ = ℤ_p[G]` is a (noncommutative in
general, commutative for `G` abelian) local ring with residue field `𝔽_p`, and consequently the
formula `mobiusWeight_free_local` applies verbatim to free `Λ`-lattices; in particular for
`Λ = ℤ_p[ℤ/pℤ]` one obtains
`#Aut(X)·#{N ≤ Λⁿ : Λⁿ/N ≅ X} = (∏_{i<d}(pⁿ - p^i))·#(𝔪X)ⁿ` for every finite `Λ`-module `X`.

*The key insight is* that the augmentation ideal of `𝔽_p[G]` is nilpotent for a `p`-group, so
`Λ/pΛ` is local and `Λ` — being module-finite over the complete local ring `ℤ_p` — inherits
locality; the Nakayama counting argument formalized here never used commutativity beyond the
`Submodule.restrictScalars` bookkeeping.

*Why now?* The counting engine is finished and ring-agnostic; the only missing ingredient is a
formal proof that `𝔽_p[G]` is local for `p`-groups, which is a self-contained nilpotence
statement about the augmentation ideal.

## D3. Non-free lattices over `ℤ_p[ℤ/pℤ]`

**Conjecture.** For `Λ = ℤ_p[ℤ/pℤ]` and *any* `Λ`-lattice `M` (including the non-projective
ones), the Möbius weight `Σ_{Y ≤ X} μ(Y,X)·#Hom(M,Y)` is a ℤ-linear combination, with
coefficients independent of `X`, of the three "free-like" weights attached to the indecomposable
lattices `ℤ_p`, `ℤ_p[ζ_p]` and `Λ`; hence the Solomon zeta function of `M` is an explicit
rational function in `p^{-s}` whose numerator degree is bounded by the number of indecomposable
summands of `M`.

*The key insight is* that `#Hom(M, Y)` is additive in `M` along direct sums, so the whole Möbius
weight is additive in the *multiplicative* sense: `mobiusWeight` for `M = ⊕Mᵢ` factors through
the multiset of `#Hom(Mᵢ, Y)`, and the classification of `Λ`-lattices into three indecomposables
turns this into a finite computation.

*Why now?* `mobiusWeight` is already known here to be a poset invariant of `X`
(`mobiusWeight_congr_right`) and a Hom-count of `M`, so the remaining input is the (finite)
representation theory of `Λ`, not any new analytic machinery.

## D4. Rationality of the refined generating function

**Conjecture.** Fix a commutative local order `R` with finite residue field and a rank `n`. Then
`Σ_X mobiusWeight R (Rⁿ) X · T^{v(X)}`, summed over isomorphism classes of finite quotient
types weighted by the length `v(X)`, is a rational function of `T` with denominator
`∏_{i=0}^{n-1}(1 - qⁱT)`, and the quotient by the maximal-order zeta function is a polynomial
with nonnegative integer coefficients.

*The key insight is* that the local formula proved here makes every coefficient a product of a
Gaussian-binomial numerator and a power of `#𝔪X`, so the generating function is a finite sum of
geometric series indexed by the residual dimension `d ≤ n`.

*Why now?* Coefficientwise integrality (`mobiusWeight`), nonnegativity (`mobiusWeight_nonneg`)
and `#Aut`-divisibility (`autCard_dvd_mobiusWeight`) are theorems; only the formal-power-series
bookkeeping and the finiteness of the set of quotient types of bounded length remain.

## D5. A Möbius-theoretic characterisation of freeness

**Conjecture.** Let `R` be a commutative local ring with finite residue field and `M` a finite
`R`-module. Then `M` is free of rank `n` **iff** for every finite `R`-module `X` the Möbius
weight `Σ_{Y ≤ X} μ(Y,X)·#Hom(M,Y)` equals `#(𝔪X)ⁿ · ∏_{i<d}(qⁿ - q^i)` with
`d = dim_k X/𝔪X`; a single well-chosen `X` (of residual dimension `n+1`) already suffices.

*The key insight is* that the local formula shows the free lattices realise the *maximal*
possible Möbius weights, and the vanishing criterion `mobiusWeight_eq_zero_iff` identifies the
minimal number of generators as the first index where the weight becomes nonzero; combining the
two turns the weight sequence into a complete invariant of freeness.

*Why now?* Both halves — the closed formula for free lattices and the generation-number
criterion — are now theorems in this development, so the conjecture is a matter of assembling
them and controlling the "only if" direction by a counting argument on `Hom(M, k)`.

### Settled in earlier cycles

The vanishing criterion `mobiusWeight_eq_zero_iff` (the least `n` for which
`Σ_{Y ≤ X} μ(Y,X)|Y|ⁿ ≠ 0` is exactly the minimal number of generators of `X`) and the coprime
Euler factorization `mobiusWeight_prod_of_coprime` were proved in the previous cycle; the
prime-power chain collapse `φ(pᵉ)·#{…} = (pᵉ)ⁿ - (p^{e-1})ⁿ` is
`totient_mul_quotIsoCount_zmod_prime_pow`.

# Future directions (next cycle)

This cycle closed all five directions carried over from the previous cycle; the
results live in `Catalog/Novelty/EulerMascheroniSharpTails.lean` and are proved
without `sorry`.  Summary of what is now available:

* `gammaTerm_lower_bound` / `gammaTerm_upper_bound`:
  `1/(2(k+2)²) ≤ gammaTerm k ≤ 1/(2(k+1)²)` (rational squeeze of every summand),
  with the sharper `gammaTerm_ge_tele : 1/(2(k+1)(k+2)) ≤ gammaTerm k`.
* `remainder_pos`, `remainder_le_inv_two_mul`:
  `0 < γ − eulerMascheroniSeq n ≤ 1/(2n)` for `n ≥ 1`.
* `tail_lower_sharp`, `tail_upper`, `abs_accelerated_error_le`,
  `accelerated_error_two_sided`: with
  `accelerated n = eulerMascheroniSeq n + 1/(2(n+1))`,
  `1/(14(n+1)²) ≤ γ − accelerated n ≤ 1/(12(n+1)²)` for **every** `n : ℕ`.
* `symKL_eq_sq_div`, `summable_symKL_iff_of_ratio_bounds`,
  `hasSum_symKL_linear_rates`, `not_summable_symKL_geometric_rates`:
  the symmetrized divergence identity, an exact summability criterion for chains
  of positive rates with bounded ratios, and its two test cases.
* `irrational_of_linear_forms`, `irrational_gamma_of_exponential_forms`,
  `accelerated_forms_do_not_decay`: the Apéry-style criterion together with a
  concrete obstruction ruling out the midpoint-accelerated family.

A second file, `Catalog/Novelty/EulerMascheroniEnclosure.lean`, turns the tail
estimate into *effective* arithmetic information about `γ`:

* `eulerMascheroniSeq_fifteen`: `eulerMascheroniSeq 15 = 1195757/360360 − 4 log 2`,
  the approximant at the first index beyond `n = 3, 7` where `log(n+1)` is an exact
  multiple of `log 2`.
* `gamma_gt`, `gamma_lt`: the certified enclosure `0.5771692 < γ < 0.5772158`
  (width `4.66·10⁻⁵`), obtained from `tail_lower_sharp 15` / `tail_upper 15` and
  Mathlib's decimal bounds for `log 2`.  The upper bound is sharp to seven decimals
  because `1/12` is the exact Euler–Maclaurin coefficient.
* `gamma_ne_div_of_den_le`, `gamma_ne_rat_of_den_le`: a finitely checked
  small-denominator obstruction — `γ ≠ p/q` for every `1 ≤ q ≤ 148`.  The threshold
  is optimal for this enclosure since `86/149 = 0.577181…` lies inside the interval.

The engine behind all of it is a family of *derivative-certificate* estimates for
`Λ(z) = log((1+z)/(1-z))` on `[0,1)`:
`2z + 2z³/3 ≤ Λ(z) ≤ min(2z/(1−z²), 2z + 2z³/3 + 2z⁵/(5(1−z²)))`,
each proved by exhibiting the derivative of the difference as an explicitly
nonnegative rational function, then evaluated at `z = 1/(2m+1)`.

Below are the next falsifiable conjectures.

---

## Conjecture 1 (Full Euler–Maclaurin ladder with rational certificates)

For every `j : ℕ` there are explicit rationals `c_1, …, c_j` (the Euler–Maclaurin
coefficients `1/2, 1/12, 0, −1/120, …`) and explicit rational constants
`a_j < b_j` such that

`a_j/(n+1)^{j+1} ≤ (−1)^j (γ − eulerMascheroniSeq n − Σ_{i≤j} c_i/(n+1)^i) ≤ b_j/(n+1)^{j+1}`

for all `n : ℕ`, and the whole ladder can be certified by the single scheme used
here: a `(2j+1)`-term `artanh` truncation for `Λ(z)` at `z = 1/(2m+1)` plus one
polynomial positivity check with positive coefficients after the shift `m = 1+s`.

**The key insight is** that every level of the Euler–Maclaurin expansion of `γ`
reduces, after the substitution `z = 1/(2m+1)`, to positivity of a *single
polynomial with nonnegative coefficients in `m − 1`* — exactly the phenomenon
observed at levels `j = 1` (numerator `2m²+2m+1`) and `j = 2` (numerator
`40(m−1)⁴+240(m−1)³+484(m−1)²+372(m−1)+73`).

**Why now?** The two levels already formalized fix the pattern, the calculus
lemmas are reusable verbatim, and the only new ingredient per level is a
mechanical polynomial-coefficient computation, so the ladder is within reach of
automation rather than requiring new mathematics.

## Conjecture 2 (Optimal constants, and a quadratically growing exclusion threshold)

For the sharp form of the acceleration error, the *best* rational constants are
`γ − accelerated n ∈ [α/(n+1)², 1/(12(n+1)²)]` with
`α = 12·(γ − 1/2) = 0.9265…/12`, i.e. the extreme cases of the two-sided bound
occur at `n = 0` (lower) and in the limit `n → ∞` (upper); equivalently the
sequence `(n+1)²(γ − accelerated n)` is strictly increasing with limit `1/12`.
Consequently, running the `EulerMascheroniEnclosure` argument at `n = 2^j − 1`
(where `log(n+1) = j·log 2` is exact) yields an enclosure of width
`Θ(4^{-j})`, hence excludes all rational denominators up to `c·4^{j}`; the
verified case `j = 4` gives the threshold `148`.

**The key insight is** that monotonicity of `(n+1)²(γ − accelerated n)` should
follow from a *single* per-term inequality of the same telescoping shape used
here, with the comparison sequence `m ↦ 1/(2m) + 1/(12m²) − ε/m³`, and that every
improvement of the pair of constants `(1/14, 1/12)` translates *linearly* into a
larger certified denominator-exclusion threshold.

**Why now?** The `Θ(n⁻²)` statement and the `j = 4` enclosure are both proved; only
monotonicity separates them from the optimal constants, and monotonicity is a
per-term inequality that the existing `logRatio` certificates can likely discharge.

## Conjecture 3 (Symmetrized tails detect exactly the `ℓ²` ratio class)

For any chain of positive rates `a : ℕ → ℝ` whose ratios `ρ n = a(n+1)/a n`
converge to `1`, the symmetrized adjacent divergences are summable **iff**
`(log ρ n)` is square-summable; and the bounded-ratio hypothesis in
`summable_symKL_iff_of_ratio_bounds` can be replaced by `ρ n → 1`.  Moreover the
total symmetrized divergence of the *harmonic* chain `a n = n+1` equals `1`
exactly (proved), while for `a n = (n+1)^p` it equals `p²·ζ(2) + O(p³)` as
`p → 0`.

**The key insight is** that `(ρ−1)²/ρ` and `(log ρ)²` are equivalent
infinitesimals of second order, so summability is a statement about the
`ℓ²`-membership of the logarithmic increments — an information-geometric
restatement of "the chain has finite Fisher length".

**Why now?** The identity `D(a‖b)+D(b‖a) = (a−b)²/(ab)` and the bounded-ratio
criterion are formalized, so only the `ρ → 1` localisation and a comparison
between `(ρ−1)²` and `(log ρ)²` remain.

## Conjecture 4 (No polynomially accurate family can prove irrationality)

Strengthening `accelerated_forms_do_not_decay`: if integer sequences `A n, B n`
with `A n + B n·γ ≠ 0` are built from any approximant family whose error is
`Θ(n^{-d})` for a fixed `d` and whose denominators grow at most polynomially,
then `|A n + B n γ|` is bounded away from `0`; consequently every Apéry-style
attack on `γ` needs approximants with super-polynomial accuracy (e.g.
hypergeometric or Nesterenko-type constructions).

**The key insight is** that the criterion `irrational_of_linear_forms` converts
irrationality into a *rate* statement, and the `Θ(n⁻²)` theorem shows the
classical accelerated harmonic family sits strictly on the wrong side of that
rate threshold.

**Why now?** Both halves — the criterion and a proved two-sided rate for a
concrete family — now exist in the same file, so the general statement can be
attacked by formalizing "polynomial denominators × polynomial error cannot beat
`1/den`".

## Conjecture 5 (Rational-certificate transfer to other Euler-type constants)

The same derivative-certificate scheme (bounds for `Λ(z)` at `z = 1/(2m+1)`,
telescoping comparison, polynomial positivity after the shift `m = 1+s`) yields
sharp two-sided `Θ(n⁻²)` acceleration bounds for the generalized Stieltjes
constants `γ_1` and for `log Γ`-type remainders (Stirling), with all constants
rational and all positivity certificates having nonnegative shifted
coefficients.

**The key insight is** that nothing in the method used `γ` itself: it only used
that the summand is `f(m) − ∫` with `f` a rational function of `m` and the
logarithm entering through `Λ(1/(2m+1))`.

**Why now?** The reusable core (`logRatio_le`, `le_logRatio`, `logRatio_le_pade`,
`hasSum_telescoping`, `hasSum_invSqTele`) is already isolated and general, so a
second constant is mostly a matter of new polynomial certificates.

# Future directions — Singmaster's problem

Derived from the analysis and adversarial review of the results now formalised in

* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterOccurrences.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterFibonacci.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterRefinements.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterParity.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterCentralBinomial.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterExactCounts.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterCentralBinomialExtended.lean`
* `Catalog/Combinatorics/SingmasterMaxBelowMillion.lean`

Notation: `N(t) = Singmaster.mult t` is the number of positions `(n,k)` with
`C(n,k) = t`.

---

## Conjecture 1 (bold). `N(t) = O(log t / log log t)`, formalisably

**Statement.** There is an absolute constant `c` with
`Singmaster.mult t ≤ c * Nat.log 2 t / Nat.log 2 (Nat.log 2 t)` for all `t ≥ 16`.

**Status here.** We proved the weaker unconditional
`Singmaster.mult_le_two_mul_log : mult t ≤ 2 * Nat.log 2 t`.

**The key insight is** that the current proof throws away everything except
"one row per column"; the Abbott–Erdős–Hanson improvement uses in addition that the
rows `n_1 > n_2 > …` attached to the distinct columns `k_1 < k_2 < …` satisfy
`n_i ≥ 2 k_i` *simultaneously*, so the multiplicative estimate
`t = C(n_i,k_i) ≥ (n_i / k_i)^{k_i}` can be applied to the **largest** column
`k_r ≥ r + 1` rather than to each column separately.

**Why now?** The whole infrastructure this needs — strict monotonicity in the row
(`choose_lt_choose_left`), strict unimodality in the column
(`choose_lt_choose_right`), the folded-index bookkeeping (`fold`, `fibre_card_le_two`)
— is already formalised and sorry-free, so only the analytic estimate
`(n/k)^k ≤ C(n,k)` remains to be added.

---

## Conjecture 2 (grand challenge). Singmaster's conjecture itself, in the
## "two rows suffice" form

**Statement.** `∃ C, ∀ t ≥ 2, Singmaster.mult t ≤ C`, and in fact `C = 8`, attained
only at `t = 3003`.

**The key insight is** the reduction proved here as
`Singmaster.two_mul_rows_card : mult t ≤ 2 * (rowsOf t).card`: since a row can carry a
given value at most twice (`row_solutions_le_two`), Singmaster's conjecture is
*equivalent* to a bound on the number of **rows** meeting the value `t`.  That
reformulation removes the column bookkeeping entirely and turns the problem into:
"how many `n` can satisfy `C(n, k_n) = t` for some `k_n`?"

**Why now?** `two_mul_rows_card` is proved and sorry-free, so the conjecture can now
be attacked in the row-only formulation; every partial result about
`(rowsOf t).card` immediately transfers to `N(t)`.

---

## Conjecture 3 (bold, cross-domain). Complete Pell classification of the
## cross-row equation

**Statement.** Every solution of `C(n,k) = C(n-1,k+1)` with `1 ≤ k ≤ n-2` is a member
of the Fibonacci family, i.e. `n = F(2i+4) F(2i+5)` and `k = F(2i+2) F(2i+5)` for
some `i ≥ 0`.  Equivalently: with `m = n - k`, the integer `(5m-1)(m-1)` is a perfect
square iff `m = F(2i+3) F(2i+5)` (or `m ∈ {1,2}`).

**Status here.** `Singmaster.choose_cross` proves the combinatorics-to-arithmetic
direction and `Singmaster.fib_cross` proves that the Fibonacci pairs are solutions.
The converse (completeness) is open in this development.

**The key insight is** that `5m^2 - 6m + 1 = \square` is, after the substitution
`x = 10m - 6`, the Pell equation `x^2 - 5y^2 = 16`, whose solution semigroup is
generated by the fundamental unit `(9 + 4\sqrt5)` of `ℤ[\sqrt5]`; Fibonacci numbers
enter exactly because that unit is `φ^6`.

**Why now?** This is a genuine algebra/combinatorics bridge: it converts a statement
about binomial coefficients into a statement about the unit group of a real quadratic
order, and Mathlib already has `Zsqrtd`, Pell equations and the Fibonacci API used in
`cassini_odd`.

---

## Conjecture 4. Central binomial coefficients have multiplicity exactly 3

**Statement.** For `m ≥ 2`, `Singmaster.mult ((2*m).choose m) = 3`.

**Status here.** Partially resolved, and pushed considerably further in this cycle.
`Singmaster.three_le_mult_centralBinom` proves `≥ 3`.  The sandwich theorem
`Singmaster.choose_lt_centralBinom` (the central entry is the strict maximum of the
triangle truncated at row `2m`) turns the conjecture into an *effective, explicitly
bounded* finite search.  Two new structural reductions shrink that search by nine orders
of magnitude: the **triangular obstruction** `Singmaster.choose_two_ne_of_not_sq`
(`C(n,2) = t` forces `8t+1` to be a square, which deletes the column `k = 2` and with it
the row window `√(2t)`, leaving `(6t)^{1/3}`) and the **column collapse**
`Singmaster.column_lt_of_choose_eq_centralBinom` (a repetition has folded column `< m`).
The resulting criterion `Singmaster.mult_centralBinom_eq_three_cubic` has been executed
in the Lean kernel for all `m ≤ 20`:
`Singmaster.mult_centralBinom_eq_three_of_le_twenty` proves `N(C(2m,m)) = 3` up to
`C(40,20) = 137846528820`.  What is still open is the uniformity in `m`.

**The key insight is** that the escape route `n > 2m` is *quadratically* bounded, not
just bounded by `t`: an interior entry satisfies `C(n,2) ≤ C(n,k) = t`, so the search
window is `2m < n < N` with `N ≈ √(2t) ≈ 2^m`.  Making that window uniformly empty is
exactly the missing step: one has to show that no row of index between `2m` and `√(2t)`
can contain `C(2m,m)`, which is a statement about the *density* of the rows of Pascal's
triangle near the value `4^m/√(πm)`.

**Why now?** The criterion is formalised and executable, so any new arithmetic input —
for instance a `p`-adic obstruction of Kummer type on the exponent of a prime `p ≤ 2m`
in `C(2m,m)` versus in `C(n,k)` — can be plugged straight into
`Singmaster.mult_centralBinom_eq_three` and immediately yields new cases (or, with a
uniform argument, the whole conjecture).

---

## Conjecture 5. No number has multiplicity exactly 5 or exactly 7

**Statement.** `∀ t, Singmaster.mult t ≠ 5 ∧ Singmaster.mult t ≠ 7`.

**Status here.** Reduced, proved conditionally, and **verified unconditionally below
`538257874440 = C(42,21)`**: `Singmaster.mult_ne_five_or_seven_of_lt_large` proves that
no `t` with `2 ≤ t < 538257874440` occurs exactly five or exactly seven times (the
earlier bound `705432` is `Singmaster.mult_ne_five_or_seven_of_lt`).  That is more than
`700000` times the range of the exploratory table of `ComputationalEvidence.md` and,
unlike the table, it is machine-checked — and it is obtained from only nineteen finite
searches, not from a scan of all `t`.  The parity criterion
`Singmaster.odd_mult_iff_centralBinom` is now a theorem: `N(t)` is odd **iff** `t` is a
central binomial coefficient `C(2m,m)`.  Hence
`Singmaster.centralBinom_of_mult_five_or_seven` shows that any `t` with `N(t) ∈ {5,7}`
is a central binomial coefficient, and
`Singmaster.no_five_or_seven_of_centralBinom_mult_three` derives the full statement
from Conjecture 4.  What remains open is exactly Conjecture 4.

**The key insight is** that the reflection `k ↦ n-k` is an involution of the occurrence
set whose only fixed points are the central entries `(2m,m)`, so
`N(t) = 2·#(left occurrences) + #(central occurrences)` with the central count at most
one — the parity of `N` is therefore a *single bit* determined by whether `t` is
central.

**Why now?** The reduction turns an unstructured search over all `t` into a question
about one explicit sequence `2, 6, 20, 70, 252, 924, …`, for which the tools already
formalised here (`row_le_of_choose_eq`, `two_pow_le_choose`, `choose_lt_choose_left`)
give an effective finite search space for each member.


---

## Next-cycle sub-conjectures (v19c thread continuation)

These are the three concrete follow-ups produced by the cycle that proved
`Singmaster.mult_eq_two_add_interior`, `Singmaster.mult_3003 = 8` and
`Singmaster.mult_ne_five_or_seven_of_lt`.

### 6a. The multiplicity is computable in `O(√t)` row tests, and `N(t) ≤ 2 + 2·log₂ √(2t)`

**Statement.** `Singmaster.mult t ≤ 2 + Nat.log 2 t` for all `t ≥ 2`.

**The key insight is** that `Singmaster.mult_eq_two_add_interior` already separates the
two *guaranteed* occurrences from the interior ones, and every interior occurrence has
folded column index `≥ 2` and lives in a row `n < √(2t)`; re-running the
column-uniqueness argument of `mult_le_two_mul_log` on the interior part alone should
save the factor two that the current bound spends on the boundary.

**Why now?** Both ingredients are theorems in this development
(`mult_eq_two_add_interior` and `fibre_card_le_two`), so this is a bookkeeping
recombination rather than new mathematics — and it would make the formal bound sharper
than the naive `2 log₂ t` for every `t`.

### 6b. `3003` is the unique number of multiplicity eight below `10^6` — **resolved**

**Statement.** For every `t` with `2 ≤ t < 10^6` and `t ≠ 3003`, `Singmaster.mult t ≠ 8`.

**Status.** Proved, in the stronger form
`Singmaster.mult_le_six_of_lt_million`: every such `t` occurs *at most six* times, so
`Singmaster.mult_eq_eight_iff_of_lt_million` gives `N(t) = 8 ↔ t = 3003` on `[2,10^6)`
and `Singmaster.mult_le_eight_of_lt_million` gives the Singmaster bound with the
conjectured optimal constant `8` on that range.  A by-product is
`Singmaster.mult_24310 = 6`, the one value of `A003015` below `10^6` that the earlier box
search could not reach.

**The key insight was** to stop quantifying over `t`.  The refined reflection
decomposition `N(t) = 2 + 2·#(left interior occurrences) + #(central occurrences)`
(`Singmaster.mult_eq_two_add_two_mul_leftInt`) plus column uniqueness means that a
multiplicity above six needs *two* left interior occurrences with column `≥ 3` and the
same value — a coincidence between two positions, not a property of a number.  There are
only `320` positions with column `≥ 3` and value below `10^6`, and comparing all `320²`
pairs in the kernel (`Singmaster.bigCols_pair_search`) shows the only coincidence is
`C(15,5) = C(14,6) = 3003`.

**Next step.** The same pair search at `10^9` or `10^{12}` is a purely quantitative
extension (the number of positions with column `≥ 3` grows like `B^{1/3}`), and the
column-`2` bookkeeping is already uniform in `B`.

### 6c. Exact multiplicity of the Fibonacci family

**Statement.** For every `i`, `Singmaster.mult (famVal i) = 6` (in particular the family
of `Combinatorics.SingmasterFibonacci` consists of numbers of multiplicity *exactly*
six, so `8` really is exceptional).

**The key insight is** that `famVal i` is not a central binomial coefficient (its
multiplicity is even by `Singmaster.odd_mult_iff_centralBinom`), so its multiplicity is
`2 · #leftOcc`; three left occurrences are exhibited by `Singmaster.fib_cross`, and a
fourth would give a second cross-row coincidence in the same value — i.e. two distinct
solutions of the Pell equation `x² - 5y² = 16` producing the same binomial value.

**Why now?** `Singmaster.mult_3003 = 8` shows the case `i = 0` is *not* six (`3003`
carries an extra triangular coincidence `C(78,2)`), so the conjecture must be stated for
`i ≥ 1`; the case `i = 1`, `famVal 1 = C(104,39)`, is a concrete falsifiable test that
the machinery of `mult_eq_two_add_interior` cannot yet reach — its box has side
`≈ 10^15` — and therefore demands the genuinely new structural input described above.

---

## Next-cycle sub-conjectures (produced by the cycle that proved
## `mult_le_eight_of_lt_million` and `mult_centralBinom_eq_three_of_le_twenty`)

### 7a. The pair search is uniform: `N(t) ≤ 8` for all `t < 10^{12}`

**Statement.** `∀ t, 2 ≤ t → t < 10^12 → Singmaster.mult t ≤ 8`, with equality only at
`t = 3003`.

**The key insight is** that `Singmaster.bigCols_pair_search` scales like `B^{2/3}` pair
comparisons, because the positions with column `≥ 3` and value `< B` number about
`(6B)^{1/3}`; the column-`2` positions never need to be enumerated at all, since column
uniqueness already caps their contribution at one.  Only the `k = 3` stratum grows, and
it can itself be handled by the cube-root analogue of the triangular obstruction:
`C(n,3) = t` iff `u³ - u = 6t` for `u = n-1`, a single candidate per `t`.

**Why now?** Every ingredient except the cube-root test is a theorem in this
development, and the `10^6` case already runs in about a minute.

### 7b. A `p`-adic obstruction makes `N(C(2m,m)) = 3` uniform in `m`

**Statement.** For all `m ≥ 2` and all `n > 2m`, `3 ≤ k < m`, one has
`C(n,k) ≠ C(2m,m)` — hence Conjecture 4 in full.

**The key insight is** that Kummer's theorem reads the exponent of a prime `p` in
`C(n,k)` off the carries of the addition `k + (n-k)` in base `p`, and `C(2m,m)` is
divisible by every prime in `(m, 2m]` exactly once (a Bertrand-type interval).  A
repetition `C(n,k) = C(2m,m)` with `k < m` therefore forces `n` to be divisible by a
prime in `(m,2m]` in a very rigid pattern, while the criterion
`Singmaster.mult_centralBinom_eq_three_cubic` already confines `n` to
`(2m, (6·C(2m,m))^{1/3})`.

**Why now?** The finite-search criterion is formalised and each new arithmetic
restriction plugs straight into it, immediately converting into new verified cases; the
searches for `m ≤ 20` are the empirical evidence that no such `n` exists.

### 7c. Multiplicity `≥ 6` forces a Pell or a genus-`≥ 1` coincidence

**Statement.** If `Singmaster.mult t ≥ 6` then either `t` belongs to the Fibonacci family
of `Combinatorics.SingmasterFibonacci`, or `t = C(n,2) = C(m,k)` for some `3 ≤ k`, i.e.
`t` is a triangular number that is also a higher binomial coefficient.

**The key insight is** the same decomposition that settled 6b: `N(t) ≥ 6` means at least
two left interior occurrences, so two distinct columns `k < k'` with `2 ≤ k`.  If `k = 2`
the value is triangular; if `k ≥ 3` the two occurrences are a coincidence between two
"deep" columns, and the `320`-element search shows that below `10^6` the only such
coincidence is the Fibonacci one, `C(15,5) = C(14,6)`.

**Why now?** The statement is a clean dichotomy that is *already verified below `10^6`*
by `Singmaster.bigCols_pair_search`, so it is falsifiable by a single new coincidence and
provable by an effective height bound on the curves `C(n,2) = C(m,k)`.
